purpose: Public methods evidence; not disclosure of proprietary production models or proof of bookmaker edge
evidence_policy: Vendor claims are first-party self-report; paper results retain original population; search-only leads are not verified citations. Local coverage counts were computed directly from archived CSVs.

professional-odds-methods.scope: Public engineering and operating disclosures from PandaScore, Oddin.gg, Abios/Kambi, GRID; current repo context from local://professional-cs2-research-contract.md. All vendor operational/model claims below are self-reports, not independent evidence of superior forecasting or profitability.
professional-odds-methods.summary: Public evidence supports a clear professional gap beyond team rating/form: rights-cleared, granular and timely match/player telemetry; a production market engine that derives multiple markets from a shared game-state probability model; separate prediction/model and odds/trading layers; human title expertise alongside automation; and operational controls for freshness, trading continuity, risk, availability and market suspension. Companies do not publish enough internals to know their actual training procedures, probability distributions, player/roster adjustment equations, or out-of-sample predictive quality. PandaScore's published round model is explicitly a CS:GO MR15 proof of concept from 2022 and not its production model or current CS2 method. It assumes Markov round dependence, models half-time pistol reset, and acknowledges close-game/stomp errors and omitted economy/map/pistol factors. CS2 MR12 materially changes the map-score process and requires refitting/re-deriving, not carrying that old 15-round structure forward. Our disclosed current model is a prematch BO3/BO5 team-level ensemble of Elo/Glicko/form/activity and static VRS, ridge C=1, side-symmetric; it is a far narrower target than operators' all-market, real-time trading stacks and has limited contemporary roster observability. The failed bookmaker challenge is not evidence of which proposed mechanism would improve it; use chronological development evidence only and retain protected TEST boundaries.

contradictions.point: Rights-holder / official data availability versus generalized access assumptions
contradictions.view_a: Vendors frame direct server data as dependable and commercially useful; e.g., GRID describes official rights partnerships and Abios names Bayes/GRID feeds.
contradictions.view_b: Rights and access are not universal/free: GRID says availability is scoped per agreement and commercial plans custom-priced; its media plan cannot serve betting products. Abios's cited feed coverage is a defined tournament set.
contradictions.resolution: Treat official feed as a purchase/rights decision and event-level coverage map, not public data access or an assumed project feature.

contradictions.point: Proprietary models versus verifiable modelling facts
contradictions.view_a: PandaScore, Oddin, Abios and GRID describe proprietary/advanced models, trader oversight and continuous refinement.
contradictions.view_b: No source discloses full production features, equations, training sample, calibration, retraining triggers/cadence, prospective log loss or independent market-beating results.
contradictions.resolution: Use disclosed architecture only as operation-level evidence; do not infer model quality or clone a private method from promotional descriptions.

contradictions.point: MR15 article versus present CS2 rules
contradictions.view_a: PandaScore's technical article describes CS:GO 15-round halves, first to 16, MR15 overtime structure and explicitly says it is a baseline.
contradictions.view_b: Valve's CS2 change specifies 12-round halves and 24-round regulation (MR12).
contradictions.resolution: The baseline gives a transferable design pattern (coherent score-state distribution), not transferable MR15 parameters/rules; any CS2 map-score model must derive current regulation/overtime and side/pistol semantics.

gaps: No independent public benchmark found for any vendor's CS2 prematch series log loss, calibration, closing-line performance or profitability; vendor turnover/uptime/margin claims are not model-performance evidence.

No public disclosure resolves actual production model families, priors, player/roster strength transfer, stand-in uncertainty, map-veto conditioning, coherent BO3/BO5 series simulation, probability calibration, or model retraining triggers/cadence.

No universally licensed free source for complete historical/current server-level CS2 telemetry established. Official data is rights-holder/event-specific and commercial terms are not published as a public rate card.
No independent substantiation for claimed sub-200ms/sub-second data latency, uptime or odds accuracy; product availability/contractual SLOs differ from headline figures.

No reliable evidence that the vendor's roster data feed proves an actual line-up-aware prediction adjustment; named sources do not publish the adjustment equations.

comparison_to_current_model.current_model_facts_from_contract: 122,038 native historical results through 2026-10-07; 23,568 modern BO3/BO5 series and 4,420 map-coded histories; model chosen from 128 candidates is ridge C=1 over team ratings/form, no recency sample weighting, mirrored and side-symmetric. Inputs include 12-series Elo, 6-map-score Elo (not map-specific), two daily Glicko-2, form/rest/activity, sparse prior measured statistics and historical VRS. Player payloads are 670 eligible series (661 in 2026), not verified contemporary starters; VRS 27 snapshots and 7-day/max(first commit clock, snapshot+7d) availability proxy. One-hour market VAL 545 eligible matches. No paid feeds, bookmaker execution claim; same-day outcomes frozen out. Broad bookmaker challenge failed; its TEST is protected.
comparison_to_current_model.strengths_relative_to_public_vendor_exam: Our coefficient training is chronological, sizeable versus scarce public quantitative vendor disclosure, avoids market prices as predictor and uses benchmark/model selection evidence with explicit temporal leakage controls. Its feature/target scope is intentionally prematch BO3/BO5 series prediction, not full live betting or per-round/player markets.
comparison_to_current_model.gaps_relative_to_professional_operations: We lack the confirmed official granular server telemetry, per-player event observations and assured release-time rights; available roster payloads do not certify active lineups. Map-specific performance is not modeled by current map-score Elo. Current learner predicts series winner without shared calibrated map/score distribution, explicit veto-conditioned market tree, or bettor exposure/risk layer. There is no 24/7 human trading operation or production feed monitoring in model evidence. Public vendor internals are confidential, so these are capabilities-level gaps, not proof that their win-probability models are superior.
comparison_to_current_model.practical_priorities: Near-term feasible: assess a coherent map-to-series probabilistic composition and stronger time-aware lineup/map-veto signals using only permitted development data; audit historic feature availability point-in-time, and label uncertainty for stale VRS/sparse roster facts. Future paid-data path: request tournament/territory/data depth/historical rights/latency/replay/derived-model-use and point-in-time timestamp terms. Add monitoring and market coverage only if product scope calls for operational betting. Do not use protected exposed TEST to choose a challenger, and do not claim independent confirmation from it.

dynamic-skill-research.scope: Fresh research beyond Elo/Glicko and EsportsBench on dynamic paired-comparison/Bayesian skill models, score-aware likelihoods, hierarchical shrinkage, uncertainty, temporal deployment, and CS2 applicability.
dynamic-skill-research.summary: Recommend a causal, sparse dynamic Bradley–Terry/logistic residual model as the next research candidate: latent name-level strengths evolve via Gaussian transitions; uncertainty grows between observations and contracts on results; the predictive probability integrates uncertainty. Start with pooled process variance and a Gaussian population prior, optionally mean-reverting only after chronological development validation. Hierarchical player effects are gated on actual, timely lineups with repeated cross-roster variation; current context does not establish these. WHR and TTT provide useful batch algorithms but smoothing uses future results and is leakage for past forecasts. Score-aware models support continuous or ordinal comparisons in general, but no inspected source validates treating stopped BO3/BO5 maps or round margins as independent fixed-length samples. Use a stopping-rule-aware BO recursion; model round/margin data with game-rule/exposure and termination structure. External results from Go, chess, Halo, NBA, ATP, and content comparisons establish method possibilities, not CS2 or bookmaker gains.

local_context.data: Contract states 122,038 native results; 23,568 modern accepted BO3/BO5 series plus 4,420 map-coded histories; 16,164 coefficient TRAIN series, 1,487 VAL; current chosen ridge C1 learner uses ratings/form among 128 candidates; 1,768 organizations and ~28k observation task scale.
local_context.rosters: Contract reports historical participant payload for 670 eligible series (661 in 2026), not verified contemporary starting rosters. Do not presume lineup availability, release time, or stable identity aliases.
local_context.experiment_protection: Existing exposed TEST is not independent confirmation; test outcomes must not tune another model. Use TRAIN/development chronological evaluation only. No model-quality experiments were run here.

design.likelihood: At forecast time t, eta = eta_existing_name-level ratings + (u_orgA,t-u_orgB,t) + any genuinely observed pre-match player terms; y_t ~ Bernoulli(sigmoid(eta)). Integrate sigmoid over the filtered Gaussian eta distribution for the predictive probability rather than using sigmoid of posterior means. Treat it as a candidate residual component/ablation, not as a bookmaker-probability copy.
design.dynamics: For elapsed time Δ, u_i,t | u_i,t-1 ~ Normal(rho^Δ u_i,t-1, q(Δ)). rho=1 is random walk (mean reversion absent); rho<1 gives mean reversion. Begin with pooled q, Gaussian prior and identifiability constraint (sum-zero contrasts); allow posterior variance to grow during inactivity. Learn q/rho and blending only on earlier chronological training predictions using proper scoring. Adaptive team/time-specific q is a higher-complexity follow-on, only if justified by chronological evidence.
design.filtering: Sequential Gaussian assumed-density/EP or Laplace update from current likelihood and predictive prior, then propagate forward. Freeze same-day outcomes as required by contract. At any historical prediction cutoff, only outcomes available before the forecast may affect the state. Bayesian posterior uncertainty matters particularly for sparse names and can be propagated into p.
design.batch alternative: WHR dynamically optimizes all time-stamped ratings with a Gaussian Wiener prior, Newton steps and per-entity tridiagonal Hessian; TTT uses repeated EP forward/backward messages. Retrospective smooth states using all outcomes can initialize analysis but cannot be used to score earlier forecast dates. For evaluation, refit/truncate by each cutoff or deploy forward filter.
design.hierarchy: Partial pooling u_i ~ Normal(mu_group,tau²) shrinks poorly observed names toward group mean. Player effects require real pre-match lineup snapshots and identification from changing lineups; do not impute rosters from organization names or historical participants. Contract's 670 payload series are limited and unverified, so broad player strength coverage is not supported.
design.series_and_score: A best-of series with target r=ceil(BO/2) should be aggregated via absorbing state DP: from nonterminal (a,b), transition to (a+1,b) with p_next and (a,b+1) with 1-p_next; stop at a=r or b=r and never observe unplayed maps. A map win is one outcome. A separate score model may use ordinal map score/round differential or an overdispersed count likelihood, but its unit is the map and it must represent MR12, overtime, and actual stopping/exposure; do not count observed rounds/maps as independent identical fixed-size trials without justification.

computational_practicality: Sparse state-space methods with fixed low-dimensional state can run in O(N) per iteration; 28k records is plausibly tractable. Kickscore paper demonstrates scale to millions; that is not a benchmark of a local implementation.

WHR paper's full analysis used 10.8m Go games/213,426 players, about 7 minutes for 200 iterations on a single 2.4GHz Core2 Duo; its per-entity tridiagonal computations are linear in appearances. Old hardware/domain-specific numbers cannot promise local runtime.

TTT paper reports 3.5m chess games and 18.5m variables/27.6m factors under 20 minutes on then-standard Pentium 4. It supports structured message passing scale, but unnecessary full history is not preferred for forward forecasts.
The 2021 GP/BRI paper evaluates 673 ATP games for 20 players and 5,904 NBA games and explicitly focuses on hindcasting; its GP MCMC is not an operational recipe for a 28k causal run.

2026 adaptive dynamic BT applies to 12,841 NBA games and reports its own lower Brier scores versus two comparators, particularly later playoffs. Domain transfer and independent replication for CS2 are unestablished.

TrueSkill2 reports Halo historical outcome accuracy 68% vs 52% classic TrueSkill. Its platform-specific massive data and kills/deaths, squads, experience, quitting are not target CS2 prematch facts; this accuracy is not log loss, betting profit or CS2 evidence.

claims.claim: Glickman's dynamic paired-comparison model evolves Gaussian skill distributions with elapsed-time variance and uses a sequential approximate Bayesian update; smoothing earlier periods explicitly conditions on future results.

contradictions.point: Dynamics model choice: random walk vs mean-reverting/adaptive dynamics
contradictions.view_a: WHR, Glickman and TrueSkill use Gaussian random-walk-like evolution; uncertainty expands with elapsed time and skill changes can go either direction.
contradictions.view_b: GP kernels allow stationary mean reversion, trends, multi-timescale variation and discontinuities; commensurate spike-slab innovation variance adapts to stable vs abrupt state periods. Added flexibility raises tuning/identification burden.

contradictions.view_a: Online models use historical information up to the forecast time, aligned to production deployment.
contradictions.view_b: WHR/TTT full history inference can revise old strengths using future results. Accurate historical curves are not valid pre-match features unless fit is truncated at each prediction cutoff.

contradictions.view_a: TrueSkill2 classic model learns from ordering, not numeric score; extra stats may be correlated or incentive sensitive.
contradictions.view_b: Generalized BT and dynamic paired-comparison models provide continuous/ordinal/Poisson/Gaussian comparison likelihoods, potentially using score data. They do not establish the correct CS2 map-round stopping model.

gaps: No inspected primary source validates CS2 round margin/map scores from an early-stopped BO3/BO5 as independent fixed-length samples. Need map/round chronology, MR12, overtime, and actual series stopping/exposure data.
Starting roster coverage, stable aliases, and point-in-time identity availability remain unverified; participant payload on 670 series is not contemporary lineup evidence.
No comparison against the project’s existing 128-candidate ridge-C1 Elo/Glicko ensemble was performed; exposed TEST must not be reused as independent evidence.
No inspected publication demonstrates bookmaker beating, CS2 profitability, or performance with this archive's release-time/identity limitations.
dynamic-skill-research.report: Recommendation for the parent: evaluate a forward-only sparse dynamic BT component on organization/name IDs, preferably as a regularized residual beside the existing ratings. Start with pooled random-walk variance, Gaussian population shrinkage and uncertainty-integrated probabilities. Use prequential log loss/Brier on chronological TRAIN/development splits to estimate transition and blending parameters; do not smooth backward across the forecast cutoff, and preserve same-day freeze rules. Add mean reversion or adaptive transitions only if justified without touching exposed TEST. Only add player effects where verified lineups exist by the prematch timestamp and provide cross-roster identifiability. Predict BO scores/series by a terminal-state recursion over map win probabilities; numeric map/round margin must be a separately specified per-map score likelihood accounting for map exposure, MR12/overtime and series termination. Evidence of scale and improvements comes from other sports/games; measured participant/roster coverage is poor, and no source supports promising bookmaker gains.

maps-roster-research.research_scope: CS2/CS:GO professional prematch forecasting: map-specific team strength, veto uncertainty, BO3/BO5 series aggregation, roster/player contributions, reusable public implementations and datasets. Research date 2026-10-10. No repository edits, local model experiments, builds, tests, lint, or formatters were performed.
maps-roster-research.comparison_to_archive: Project facts per local contract: 122,038 native results through 2026-10-07; modern accepted history 23,568 BO3/BO5 series, 4,420 map-coded histories; current ridge C1 uses ratings/form, and the map-score Elo bank is not map-specific. Actual archive identifiers/schema and overlap with the external data were not available in the provided contract, so match-level joinability and new row yield remain unverified. Hugging Face OpenCS2 exposes native HLTV match_id, UTC match_date, event/team names, map_index/map_name, and CS2 player SteamIDs; HLTV endpoint also exposes native match/team/event/map-stat IDs. Join on native match id first where possible, then verify participants/date/map; do not treat team display names as stable IDs or assume coverage/release timestamps.

map_team_rating.minimum_table: map_result(match_id, played_at_utc, team1_id, team2_id, map_id/name, map_winner_id; optionally regulation/OT round scores, side starts, event/game/version)
map_team_rating.candidate: Chronological dynamic Bradley-Terry/logistic model: logit P(A beats B on map m)= (team global strength A - B) + (map-specific team deviations A,m - B,m), with map deviations partially pooled toward zero. Optional time evolution on global and map terms; use only pre-match state. This is a proposed feasible model, not a performance guarantee. Validate against global Elo/map-neutral baseline on chronological development data.
map_team_rating.caveat: Pikhart thesis supports map-dependent skill/effects and score-driven/common-opponent forecasting, but is CS:GO MR15 era and reports accuracy, not log-loss. No inspected source established that a hierarchical CS2 map strength term improves prematch log-loss in this archive.

pre_veto.minimum_table: match(match_id, timestamp, event/tournament, team IDs, best_of, legal_map_pool_as_of_event); veto_step(match_id, ordered_step, acting_team_id|null, action, map); maps(match_id, played_order, map, picker|null, played, winner/score)
pre_veto.candidate: Fit a conditional choice/softmax model per legal veto state using available maps, step, actor/team, opponent, and point-in-time global/map strengths and lineup features; hard-mask illegal actions. Enumerate or sample legal veto sequences to produce P(veto|x), then integrate series probability across veto sequences rather than plug in one modal veto. Once per-map p values are available, a shared latent team/day form or posterior draw can create coherent dependence; map outcomes need not be assumed independent. BO3/BO5 match-absorption dynamic programming computes series chance from map probabilities and sequence.
pre_veto.distinction: Petri et al. is counterfactual veto policy optimization/off-policy evaluation, not evidence that a behavior model forecasts the actual chosen sequence better, and its claimed probability gains concern hypothetical policy rewards, not held-out prediction log-loss. Train actual-veto choices for predictive sequence probabilities; keep optimal-strategy analysis separately labeled.
pre_veto.caveat: Veto step rules, event map pool, side/decider rules, and available maps vary by match/tournament/era. Do not infer the legal pool or sequence from a present-day generic rule. Do not invent veto-release clocks: the sources establish match date, not when each veto became public/known.

player_and_lineup.minimum_table: map_player(match_id, played_at_utc, map_id, native_player_id such as SteamID/HLTV player id, team_id, participation/starting-five evidence, per-map contribution outcomes); roster spells(player_id, team_id, start/end effective timestamps plus source/provenance); map team outcomes and opponents. Role/side/economy/action context required for contextual action-value models.
player_and_lineup.candidate: First implement dated verified lineup aggregation of persistent player priors, with missing/uncertain lineup represented as uncertainty rather than guessed roster. Add regularized adjusted plus-minus on map/team outcome or round-margin labels, with team/opponent/player effects; paired with hierarchical shrinkage and chronological evaluation. Continuity can enter as prior shared maps / tenure / changes only when those facts are timestamped. Roles require independently sourced role/exposure labels or demo-level duties, with partial pooling; do not hardcode role bonuses.
player_and_lineup.caveat: Plus-minus paper proposes linear/logistic/Bayesian rating models but abstract alone does not establish forecast gains. Team-switching case study finds initial declines followed by recovery, but this is observational association and not universal roster penalty. Rating 3.0/action values and HLTV stats are post-map outcomes: useful as historical lagged player features, never as prematch same-match inputs.

minimum_inputs_and_candidates.series_dependence: No inspected source establishes a validated prematch inter-map dependence model for CS2 BO3/BO5. Separate map-specific matchup strength from stochastic series-level latent strength/uncertainty; integrate through dynamic programming or Monte Carlo over posterior rating draws. Map outcomes' conditional independence is a modeling assumption, not an evidenced fact.

sources_reviewed.title: Bandit Modeling of Map Selection in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive
sources_reviewed.evidence: Over 3,500 CS:GO BO3 matches and 25,000+ decisions; legal-map availability and each team's all-map/map-specific win rates are context; softmax policy gradient; off-policy direct-method and self-normalized importance weighting. The paper itself says its conclusions vary drastically between evaluators and SN-IW can be imprecise far from logging policy. Historical CS:GO pool and MR15; counterfactual strategy, not series-log-loss model.
sources_reviewed.quote: The direct method instead of the self-normalized estimator, we reach drastically different conclusions about which model to use

sources_reviewed.title: Prediction models in e-sports: Generalized autoregressive score and common opponent models
sources_reviewed.kind: 2019 University of Economics Prague master's thesis, full PDF
sources_reviewed.evidence: CS:GO result forecasting from publicly available match time/result; map-independent and map-dependent GAS plus general/map-specific/time-weighted common-opponent approaches; temporal team skill. Thesis describes 2019 standard CS:GO MR15 and seven-map veto system, so its game mechanics are era-bound. Reported best accuracy table uses differing sample sizes and is accuracy, not log loss. More detailed data/evaluation pages should be inspected before any reproduction.
sources_reviewed.quote: The most significant advantage shared by both of these models ... is that they require only publicly available data in order to forecast future match results.

sources_reviewed.title: Rating Players of Counter-Strike: Global Offensive Based on Plus/Minus value
sources_reviewed.evidence: CS:GO plus-minus player rating explores regularized linear regression, logistic regression and Bayesian linear models against team point differences; proposes indirect contribution measurement. Abstract provides no independently verified effect size/forecast benchmark; supplemental public implementation/data availability was not established here.
sources_reviewed.quote: Using models such as regularized linear regression, logistic regression, and Bayesian linear models, we examine the relationship between player participation and team point differences.

sources_reviewed.title: Individual and Collective Performance Deteriorate in a New Team: A Case Study of CS:GO Tournaments
sources_reviewed.evidence: Observational CS:GO tournament study reports player/team performance declines initially after player switches and later recovery. It motivates testing a time-varying adaptation feature, not a fixed adjustment; not a prematch log-loss paper and not causal proof that any roster switch produces a particular penalty.
sources_reviewed.quote: After a player switched to a new team, both the individual and the collective performance dropped initially, and then slowly recovered.

sources_reviewed.title: Valuing Player Actions in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive
sources_reviewed.evidence: Context-aware action valuation based on changes in round-win chance; reports open-source data model/parser and 70m+ in-game events. This is live/round-state action attribution from demos, not directly prematch. Potential lagged player summaries can be calculated before forecast date if source data/IDs are licensed and available.
sources_reviewed.quote: a context-aware framework to value players' actions based on changes in their team's chances of winning.

sources_reviewed.title: HLTV CS2 Demos Dataset
sources_reviewed.kind: public dataset card and metadata schema; maintainer-provided
sources_reviewed.evidence: One Parquet row per played CS2 .dem/map. Fields include HLTV match_id, event, team1/team2, series format, UTC match_date, map_index/map_name, patch, played rounds, winner side; nested player name and SteamID and player K/D/ADR/KAST/rating/impact; round/kills detail. Maps played only, not full legal pool or veto decisions. Card says demos mirrored from HLTV public endpoint and downstream users must respect tournament terms. Current README examples contain old repo IDs while repository card is current, so check actual file paths/revision before ingestion.
sources_reviewed.quote: Each row of the metadata Parquet is one .dem file (one played CS2 map)

sources_reviewed.title: HLTV Rating 3.0 methodology
sources_reviewed.evidence: Explains economy adjustment and round swing using map/side/economy/players-alive/bomb context, with kill credit apportioned by damage, flash assists and trades. Rich contextual player measurements, but produced during matches; no claim here of prematch forecast lift or source code/reproducibility. Good conceptual blueprint only if equivalent historic demo inputs are available.
sources_reviewed.quote: Round Swing looks at each kill and sees how much it changes a team's chance of winning the round.

sources_reviewed.title: HLTV match endpoint types and parser
sources_reviewed.evidence: Defines FullMatch with native numeric match ID, optional Unix date, event, optional teams with IDs, vetoes whose action enum is removed/picked/leftover and optional acting team, maps with map name/stat ID/round scores/half results, and players. Scraper extracts veto lines in page order. This is a collection schema/parser, not a downloadable dataset or guarantee of completeness/stability; HLTV scraping constraints/terms need separate review. Presence of `date` is not a veto disclosure time.
sources_reviewed.quote: export interface Veto { team?: Team; map: GameMap; type: 'removed' | 'picked' | 'leftover' }

sources_reviewed.title: CS2 Major ML Pick'Em Predictor
sources_reviewed.kind: public implementation and documented example schemas; author-reported
sources_reviewed.evidence: Implements map-level XGBoost + isotonic model, time-weighted/Beta-smoothed features, veto softmax simulation, Monte Carlo. Readme specifies match CSV with HLTV match_id/type/teams/series score/date/url; player map/side rows with player id, kills/deaths/ADR/KAST/rating; match detail ordered veto_steps and map picker/score/winner/half-side. Crawler is explicitly unpublished; examples are not full training data. Claims test/backtest/validation are self-reported and no independent guarantee. Team-name exact-match fallback to 0.5 is a brittle identity lesson.
sources_reviewed.quote: The crawler is not convenient to publish, so everyone can scrape the data by themselves.

sources_reviewed.title: CS2 Dynamic Hybrid Elo Tournament Forecaster
sources_reviewed.evidence: Documented V2 replays map records point-in-time, combines org/team Elo (180d half-life) and player Elo aggregated across active five (1095d half-life), has lineup-prior-map/cold-start features, logistic/XGBoost map predictions and BO3/BO5 simulations; repository includes input/features/artifacts. README explicitly says held-out evaluation one-shot and details leakage controls, but project has no stars and results are self-reported. Inspecting this is high-value implementation reference, not independent proof; roster inputs require active-five evidence and timestamped data.
sources_reviewed.quote: The pipeline replays valid maps in strict chronological order. Every feature is emitted before the current result updates state.

evaluation_and_boundaries: Prematch prediction inputs must have as-of timestamps and known-at time. Post-veto probability is a distinct forecast after actual picks/bans are observed; map/round/demo outcomes are never prematch inputs.

Keep veto sequence prediction (behavioral conditional likelihood) apart from strategy optimization (counterfactual policy utility). Paper's policy reward improvement is not calibrated predictive log-loss and depends on off-policy evaluator; paper says direct-method vs SN-IW conclusions diverge.

Series outcomes couple maps through shared opponent strength, lineup/day form, and map order context. A BO3/BO5 recursion is a calculation from supplied per-map conditional probabilities, not evidence of conditional independence. Compare no-dependence baseline vs shared rating posterior draws using chronological development only.

For fair CS:GO-to-CS2 transport, use a game-version/era indicator or distinct latent parameters; legacy paper's CS:GO rules/pool and demo data are not automatically CS2-ready. Current MR12 economy and map pool change.

For HLTV rating/action features: lag and timestamp source statistics before match date; these ratings are completed-match evaluation metrics and are not known before that match. Role labels from editorial attributes are not automatically historically complete or point-in-time.

No public source inspected supplied verified contemporary starting five with trusted release timestamps, complete veto data over the project's history, permission assurance covering redistribution, or verified external-to-local archive join yield. Don't infer announcement/release times from match times or page scrape timestamps.
maps-roster-research.recommendation: Feasible low-risk follow-on candidate (parent determines experiment): build only well-defined native-ID historical joins from OpenCS2 metadata to local archive; produce map-level rows with event timestamps and raw source provenance, explicitly noting post-match data. Separately test hierarchical/partial-pooled map residuals against current team-strength baseline and a legal-pool veto marginalization model only where actual ordered veto records and event-specific legal pool are present. Do not add sparse demo-derived player stats or unverified rosters as automatic predictors. For player channel, treat verified dated active-five priors and regularized player/opponent-adjusted outcome model as a distinct hypothesis. Any measured comparison should be chronological and use non-exposed development/validation evidence; no independent confirmation claim from prior locked/exposed test.

local_data_audit.scope: coverage/provenance only; no new TEST probabilities or scores

opencs2.score_correction: Export score1/score2 are series scores, not per-map scores; analysis_score_ct/t are side counts, not stable-organization scores. Valid per-map labels require reconstruction and independent organization orientation.
